title: Release Kitchen: sprint recipe and smoke-tasting notes
body:
Context
This is a working doc that frames the next sprint's production deployment as a 'kitchen' exercise — recipes (checklists) for each stage, a tasting panel (smoke tests + quick quality checks), and a serving calendar (rollout windows). Goal is to have a small, repeatable deployment ritual for weekday microdeploys and one larger weekend release.

High-level goals
- Zero-surprise cutover: clear owner for each lane, concise preflight, and a 30-minute smoke tasting after traffic shift.
- Telemetry-first: each recipe includes the top 6 metrics to watch + sampling guidance.
- Fast rollback path: one-card checklist to restore previous routing and capacity.

Mise en place (preflight checklist — recipe base)
- Sanity: merge queue is empty, release branch is built and artifacts verified (sha in release note).
- Config: feature flags defined and reviewed, rollout percentages set in console.
- Capacity: dedicated pool nodes provisioned (x machines), autoscaler warmup verified.
- Infra: infra-tenant certs valid, DNS TTL documented, region-level fallbacks confirmed.
- Data: migration window planned (if any), read-only fallback verified.
- Observability: dashboards pinned, SLO targets annotated, alert thresholds staged (non-actionable during initial 5m).
- Communications: #release-kitchen Slack channel created, on-call pager rota confirmed, postmortem owner assigned.
- Linked checks: small e2e smoke harness run against staging with seed requests (link above).

Rollout Calendar (serving windows)
- Week-of deploy (microdeploy lanes): 2026-03-22 to 2026-03-26 — daily slot at 10:30 PT (low-traffic local window).
  - 10:30 PT: quick preflight (15m), deploy (5–10m), 30m smoke tasting.
- Friday small-batch: 2026-03-26 13:00 PT — expanded test windows, extended smoke (60m).
- Weekend major release: 2026-03-28 02:00 PT — deep preflight earlier on Friday, weekend staffing includes SRE + release engineer.

Deployment recipe (step-by-step)
1) Preflight (owner: release chef) — confirm Mise en place checklist is green.
2) Dry-run deploy to shadow pool (owner: deploy baker) — validate startup metrics.
3) Canary gust (10% traffic) to new variant for 20m (owner: traffic shepherd).
   - Watch list (primary tasting metrics): p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, reject ratio, queue depth, memory RSS, GPU utilization.
4) If green, roll to 50% over 10 minutes, then 100% (staggered by region).
5) After 100% mark, start 30m tasting window. Collect quick snapshots and tasting notes.

Smoke-tasting notes template (what to capture)
- Time: 2026-03-22 10:48 PT
- Tester(s): Dana Chen, Miguel Ortega
- Quick health: all APIs responding, no 5xx spikes in first 5m (pass/fail).
- Observed anomalies: small increase in kv cache misses localized to us-west-2 (investigate).
- Actions: enabled cache-prefill for nightshift (PR #234), continue 30m watch.

Rollback recipe (single-card)
- Trigger threshold: sustained 5xx > 0.5% for 10m OR p95 latency > target by 2x for 15m.
- Steps: 1) Pause rollout in console. 2) Route traffic back to previous variant (routing button + verify). 3) Scale up previous pool to handle traffic (if needed). 4) Post a short note to #release-kitchen and Page SRE. 5) Start incident bridge if rollback fails.

Observability checklist (tasting panel)
- Dashboards: release_kitchen/summary, release_kitchen/latency, release_kitchen/errors, release_kitchen/resource.
- Alerts: create temp suppression for noisy non-actionable alerts, keep SRE-notify for high-sev.
- Logs: set query for recent deploy sha and sample 10 request traces.
- Traces: collect 3 traces for typical slow path and one for cold-start path.
- Cost telemetry: quick check token burn rate vs baseline for first 30m.

Night-of/Weekend specifics
- Deep smoke tasting (60–120m). Bring the tasting panel (Dev lead + SRE + Product).
- Fallback lanes: queued fallback to regional model variant if global model latency degrades.
- Escalation ladder: release chef -> SRE lead -> Eng manager -> Incident commander.

Runbook snippets (copyable)
- Verify current variant: curl -H "x-release-sha: $(cat RELEASE_SHA)" https://health-check.internal/release
- Route-back quick: infra-console -> Routing -> select previous SHA -> set 100% -> confirm.
- Capture snapshots: /tools/snapshot --dash release_kitchen/summary --out /tmp/release-snap-$(date +%s).json
(Notes: some commands are shorthand and will need exact paths in prod ops shell)

Open questions / TODOs
- Which quiet-window is safest for APAC customers? (Priya to analyze traffic heatmap, due 2026-03-12).
- Can we automate the 10%->50% step into a single button for weekday microdeploys? (Marco exploring console change).
- Add a lightweight smoke harness that runs sample prompts through the latest model variant — who owns it? (Elena to prototype).

Notes to self (working thoughts)
- Keep tasting windows short for frequent deploys to avoid alert fatigue; extend only for larger changes.
- Borrowed idea: pre-warm model caches by replaying top-100 prefixes before routing. Works well in staging, need small canary in prod.

Appendix: release note draft (short)
Title: Small weekday enhancements and stability tweaks (2026-03-22)
Summary: Rolling out routing and cache changes aimed at reducing p95 latency for short contexts and improving throughput for dedicated pools. No migrations.
Impact: Expect transient small increase in cache miss rates during initial 10–20 minutes in affected regions; fall back automatically if errors spike.
Owners: Dana Chen (release chef), Miguel Ortega (deploy baker), Priya Singh (telemetry).
Linked: jira/RELEASE-789, PR #234

If this format works, I will:
- turn the tasting template into a lightweight Google Form so we capture structured notes across releases,
- bake the single-card rollback into the console quick actions, and
- add the pre-warm job to the daily staging cadence.
